[[File:Hermann Amand Schwarz (1843-1921) by Louis Zipfel.jpg|thumb|[[Hermann Schwarz]], c. 1890]]
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] theory of [[special function]]s, '''Schwarz's list''' or the '''Schwarz table''' is the list of 15 cases found by {{harvs|txt|first=Hermann|last=Schwarz|authorlink=Hermann Schwarz|year=1873|loc=p. 323}} when [[hypergeometric function]]s can be expressed algebraically. More precisely, it is a listing of parameters determining the cases in which the [[hypergeometric equation]] has a finite [[monodromy group]], or equivalently has two independent solutions that are [[algebraic function]]s. It lists 15 cases, divided up by the [[isomorphism class]] of the monodromy group (excluding the case of a [[cyclic group]]), and was first derived by Schwarz by methods of complex analytic geometry. Correspondingly the statement is not directly in terms of the parameters specifying the hypergeometric equation, but in terms of quantities used to describe certain [[spherical triangle]]s.

The wider importance of the table, for general second-order differential equations in the [[complex plane]], was shown by [[Felix Klein]], who proved a result to the effect that cases of finite monodromy for such equations and [[regular singularities]] could be attributed to changes of variable (complex analytic mappings of the [[Riemann sphere]] to itself) that reduce the equation to hypergeometric form. In fact more is true: Schwarz's list underlies all second-order equations with regular singularities on compact [[Riemann surface]]s having finite monodromy, by a pullback from the hypergeometric equation on the Riemann sphere by a complex analytic mapping, of degree computable from the equation's data.<ref>A modern treatment is in {{cite journal
 | last1 = Baldassarri | first1 = F.
 | last2 = Dwork | first2 = B. |author-link2=Bernard Dwork
 | doi = 10.2307/2373938
 | issue = 1
 | journal = American Journal of Mathematics
 | mr = 527825
 | pages = 42–76
 | title = On second order linear differential equations with algebraic solutions
 | volume = 101
 | year = 1979| jstor = 2373938
 }}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Baldassari | first = F.
 | journal = Groupe de travail d'analyse ultramétrique
 | page = Exposé no. 22, 17 pp
 | title = Towards a Schwarz list for Lamé's differential operators via division points on elliptic curves
 | url = https://archive.numdam.org/item/GAU_1986-1987__14__A12_0/
 | volume = 14
 | year = 1986–1987}}; see pp. 5-6.</ref>

The numbers <math>\lambda, \mu, \nu</math> are (up to permutations, sign changes and addition of <math>(\ell,m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}^3</math> with <math>\ell+m+n</math> even) the differences <math>1-c, c-a-b,b-a</math> of the exponents of the [[hypergeometric differential equation]] at the three singular points <math>0,1,\infty</math>. They are rational numbers if and only if <math>a,b</math> and <math>c</math> are, a point that matters in arithmetic rather than geometric approaches to the theory.

==Further work==
An extension of Schwarz's results was given by T. Kimura, who dealt with cases where the [[identity component]] of the [[differential Galois group]] of the hypergeometric equation is a [[solvable group]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Kimura | first = Tosihusa
 | journal = Funkcialaj Ekvacioj
 | mr = 277789
 | pages = 269–281
 | title = On Riemann's equations which are solvable by quadratures
 | url = https://fe.math.kobe-u.ac.jp/FE/Free/vol12/fe12-18.pdf
 | volume = 12
 | year = 1969–1970}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Morales-Ruiz | first1 = Juan J.
 | last2 = Ramis | first2 = Jean Pierre
 | doi = 10.4310/MAA.2001.v8.n1.a5
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Methods and Applications of Analysis
 | mr = 1867496
 | pages = 113–120
 | title = A note on the non-integrability of some Hamiltonian systems with a homogeneous potential
 | volume = 8
 | year = 2001| doi-access = free
 }}; see p. 116 for the formulation.</ref> A general result connecting the differential Galois group ''G'' and the monodromy group &Gamma; states that ''G'' is the [[Zariski closure]] of &Gamma; &mdash; this theorem is attributed in the book of Matsuda to [[Michio Kuga]]. By general differential [[Galois theory]], the resulting Kimura-Schwarz table classifies cases of integrability of the equation by algebraic functions and [[Numerical integration|quadrature]]s.

Another [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Arithmetic triangle group|relevant list is that of K. Takeuchi]], who classified the (hyperbolic) [[triangle group]]s that are [[arithmetic group]]s (85 examples).<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Takeuchi | first = Kisao
 | doi = 10.2969/jmsj/02910091
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan
 | mr = 429744
 | pages = 91–106
 | title = Arithmetic triangle groups
 | volume = 29
 | year = 1977| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

[[Émile Picard]] sought to extend the work of Schwarz in complex geometry, by means of a [[generalized hypergeometric function]], to construct cases of equations where the monodromy was a [[discrete group]] in the [[projective unitary group]] ''PU''(1, ''n''). [[Pierre Deligne]] and [[George Mostow]] used his ideas to construct [[lattice (group theory)|lattices]] in the projective unitary group. This work recovers in the classical case the finiteness of Takeuchi's list, and by means of a characterisation of the lattices they construct that are arithmetic groups, provided new examples of non-arithmetic lattices in ''PU''(1, ''n'').<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://archive.numdam.org/ARCHIVE/PMIHES/PMIHES_1986__63_/PMIHES_1986__63__5_0/PMIHES_1986__63__5_0.pdf|title = Monodromy of hypergeometric functions and non-lattice integral monodromy|journal = Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS|year = 1986|volume = 63|pages = 5–89|last1 = Deligne|first1 = Pierre|last2 = Mostow|first2 = G. D.|doi = 10.1007/BF02831622|s2cid = 121385846}}</ref>

Baldassari applied the Klein universality, to discuss algebraic solutions of the [[Lamé equation]] by means of the Schwarz list.<ref>F. Baldassarri, ''On algebraic solutions of Lamé's differential equation'', J. Differential Equations 41 (1) (1981) 44–58. Correction in [http://math.arizona.edu/~rsm/papers/paper104.pdf ''Algebraic Solutions of the Lamé Equation, Revisited'' (PDF)], by Robert S. Maier.</ref>

Other hypergeometric functions which can be expressed algebraically, like those on Schwarz's list, arise in theoretical physics in the context of <math>T \overline{T}</math> deformations of two-dimensional gauge theories.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brennan| first1=T. Daniel| last2=Ferko| first2=Christian|  last3=Sethi| first3=Savdeep| title=A non-abelian analogue of DBI from ''T{{overline|T}}'' | journal=SciPost Physics| year=2020| volume=8| issue=4| page=052| doi=10.21468/SciPostPhys.8.4.052|arxiv=1912.12389 | s2cid=209515455| doi-access=free}}</ref>
